title: Abyssal Cycles: Offline RPG — building a turn-based dark fantasy game in Godot with Codex (mostly Sol 6.1 Ultra & Astra)
author: Human-Director-4494
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m the developer of Abyssal Cycles: Offline RPG, a dark fantasy game for Android with turn-based combat and a portrait layout.

You choose a character class and develop your build through active techniques, passive abilities and equipment. From camp, you head out on expeditions, face enemies and collect loot. Between adventures, you return to prepare your character, improve your equipment at the forge and decide which skills to take into the next fight. The game also includes a campaign, and the gameplay works offline.

On the development side, I’m using Godot and Codex. One concrete part of my AI workflow has been setting up project-specific instructions for the UI. These cover implementing mockups as actual Godot controls and reusable components, keeping fonts and navigation consistent, and comparing rendered screens against the references. That gives the assistant specific constraints to follow as the different screens evolve.

I’d love to hear what you think about the combat and character progression. I’m also happy to discuss the Godot and Codex workflow with anyone working on a similar project.

[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.abyssalcycles.game)
